newsitem.title: UK: IRA says it killed British soldier.
newsitem.headline: IRA says it killed British soldier.

text.p: The Irish Republican Army (IRA ) said on Thursday one of its snipers fired the bullet that killed a British soldier two weeks ago, marking an escalation in the group's guerrilla war against British rule over Northern Ireland.

The IRA said in a statement members of its hardline "South Armagh Brigade" were responsible for the attack on Stephen Restorick, 23, as he spoke to a motorist at a checkpoint near a heavily fortified military helicopter base at Bessbrook, close to the Irish border, on February 12.
British security forces on Thursday disarmed a powerful mortar bomb abandoned by guerrillas after a failed attack on police and troops in Irish nationalist west Belfast.
Police Superintendent Ian Williamson said civilians could have been injured if the mortar bomb had exploded.
The mortar bomb was found near a security base overlooking the busy Falls Road after the IRA told news organisations it had failed to detonate.
"This device...was live, fully primed and exceedingly dangerous," Williamson told a news conference.
The IRA 's statement was published in An Phoblacht, the weekly newspaper of its Sinn Fein political wing.
"One of the (British) soldiers on duty was hit by a single shot and died," it said.
Restorick was the second British soldier to be killed by republican guerrillas in the province since October.
A woman civilian who was speaking to Restorick when he was shot narrowly escaped serious injury. Her head was grazed.
The killing sparked outrage in London, Dublin and Washington and led to mounting calls for the IRA to abandon its war unconditionally.
IRA violence in recent months has provoked three attacks on Catholic nationalists by pro-British Loyalist militants. British security sources say a Loyalist truce remains in force but is shaky.
Sinn Fein wants an immediate seat at all-party talks on the future of the province, but Britain insists the IRA must end its guerrilla campaign first.
